paper.title: Learning from Logged Implicit Exploration Data

settings.name_in_paper: Warm start problem for contextual exploration (offline policy evaluation/selection from logged data)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline (batch) learning from logged contextual bandit data generated by unknown, possibly deterministic logging policies; no online interaction or cumulative regret.
unmapped: Data logged by a sequence of T fixed, possibly deterministic, unknown logging policies pi_1..pi_T
Learner estimates the logging propensity pi_hat by regression and uses a threshold tau on importance weights
Comparator is the best policy in a finite class H with adequate support (pi(h(x)|x) > tau for all x)
settings.definition_quote: An instance of the {\it contextual bandit problem} is specified by a distribution $D$ over tuples $\left(x,\vec{r}\right)$ ... Formally, given a dataset of the form $S = (x,a,r_a)^*$ generated by the interaction of an uncontrolled logging policy, we want to construct a policy $h$ maximizing ... $V^h := E_{(x,\vec{r})\sim D}[ r_{h(x)} ]$.

algorithms.name: Empirical value maximization with thresholded estimated-propensity importance weighting

symbols.reg_bar: E_x[reg(x)], reg(x)=max_a (pi(a|x)-pi_hat(a|x))^2: squared error of the propensity estimate
symbols.N_exp: |H|, size of the finite policy class

conditions: H is a finite set of deterministic policies
comparator h_tilde is the best policy in H with pi(h(x)|x) > tau for all x
logging policies do not depend on the evaluation data

source.label: t:opt
source.quote: Let $\hat\pi$ be any function from $X$ to distributions over actions $A$. Let $\cal H$ be any set of deterministic policies. Define $\tilde{\cal H} = \{ h\in\mathcal{H}~|~\pi(h(x)|x) > \tau, ~\forall ~x \in X \}$ and $\tilde{h} = \argmax_{h \in \tilde{ \mathcal{H} }} \{ V^h \}$. Let $\hat{h} = \argmax_{h \in {\mathcal{H}}} \{ \hat{V}_{\hat\pi}^{h} \}$ ... Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $V^{\hat{h}} \geq V^{\tilde{h}} - \frac{2}{\tau}\left( \sqrt{\EE_x[\reg(x)]} + \sqrt{\frac{\ln(2|H|/\delta)}{2T}} \right)$

results.notes: Bound on value gap V^{h_tilde} - V^{h_hat} (simple-regret-like) of the learned policy vs best supported policy in H; recorded as quantity 'other'. T is the number of logged samples.

symbols.reg_bar: E_x[reg(x)], squared error of the propensity estimate

conditions: h deterministic with pi(h(x)|x) >= tau for all x

source.label: c:res_est
source.quote: Let $\hat\pi$ be any function from $X$ to distributions over actions $A$. Let $h:X \to A$ be any deterministic policy. If $\pi(h(x)|x) \geq \tau$ for all inputs $x$, then $|\EE[\hat{V}_{\hat\pi}^h]-V^h| \leq \frac{\sqrt{\EE_x[\reg(x)]}}{\tau}$.

results.notes: Bias bound of the off-policy value estimator (policy evaluation). Lemma 3.1 gives a related two-sided bias bound with indicator terms; not recorded separately.
